newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall, bonds rise, dollar ends mixed.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall, bonds rise, dollar ends mixed.

text.p: Stocks fell for the second straight session Thursday as technology issues took a beating, while bond prices rose and the dollar ended mixed.
Coffee prices rose to fresh 20-year highs on persistent supply worries. Oil and gold both edged higher.

The Dow Jones industrial average dropped 27.05 points to 7,330.18 after falling 26 points Wednesday on the New York Stock Exchange. But in the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,435 to 1,043 on modest volume of 460.5 million shares.
The Nasdaq market's technology-laden composite index slid 7.14 points to 1,403.04.
Investors turned up the pressure on technology stocks, which had provided much of the market's recent strength.
International Business Machines Corp. tumbled 2-1/4 to 87-7/8, and computer network company stocks were hit after big recent gains.

"A lot of these tech stocks had made ferocious runs in a very volatile market," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Wall Street always tends to go to extremes, and there's always a snap back afterwards."
With many major indexes near record highs, analysts said they detected a cautious mood among investors.
Several key economic reports are due over the next week, they noted, which also prodded investors to lock in profits from the market's six-week surge.
"We have a couple of pieces of data coming up that are going to be very important," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Next week, the government will issue the May jobs report and the nation's purchasing managers will report on industrial activity in June.

Friday, the government will revise its initial reading of the economy's first-quarter performance, a report likely to draw attention because of the strong growth already recorded. Economists forecast a revision to a 6.0 percent annual growth rate for the quarter from the initial 5.6 percent rate.
Some analysts wondered if even those forecasts, which are more than double the growth rate the Federal Reserve is believed to target, are high enough.
The Fed decided on May 20 to leave interest rates unchanged after raising short-term rates a quarter point in March in a bid to slow the economy and ward off inflation.

Worries about higher rates failed to shake bond traders, as the market turned in a solid performance. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 20/32, or $6.25 on a $1,000 bond, cutting its yield to 6.98 percent from 7.03 percent on Wednesday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.

In currency markets, the dollar rose against the yen after Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry reported the country's industrial output fell 0.4 percent in April. Private economists had expected it to rise.

The dollar stood at 116.18 yen late in New York, up from 115.85 yen late Wednesday. The dollar also rose to 1.6965 German marks from 1.6956 marks. But it fell to 1.4105 Swiss francs from 1.4111 and to Canadian $1.3805 from C$1.3828.
At the Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange in New York, the sizzling rally in coffee prices carried into a third straight session with prices shattering the $3-a-pound barrier.
Coffee for July delivery rose 19.25 cents to $314.80 a pound after hitting $3.18, the highest price for coffee on the exchange in two decades.

"We are seeing history happen," said Christian Wolthers, vice president of Miami-based importer Blaser & Wolthers Speciality Coffee Trading Co. "We've not seen a market move like this without frost, drought or any other kind of tragedy. It is a clear situation of short supply for demand."
July crude oil rose 18 cents to $20.97 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange and August gold added $1 to $348.60 an ounce at New York's Commodity Exchange.
